properties.Name: 9/16/18 21:53  Train derailment near Lilesville.
properties.Description: CSX Train Derailment near Lilesville. One car leaking, limited risk with long term exposure. Area evacuated. SUMMARY: On 16 Sep 18 at approximately 1800 EDT, the National Response Center (NRC) reported the derailment of nine locomotives and ten rail cars near mile post SF 270.1 in Lilesville, NC:•	One hazardous material car is smoking and reportedly carrying Butyraldehyde.	Butyraldehyde is a flammable liquid which can be a minor health hazard if exposed to it for prolonged periods.•	Several other cars are carrying chemicals or oils, but none have been reported as leaking or spilled.•	Initial indications are the derailment may have been caused by effects of heavy rainfall and possible washout undermining track integrity.	Officials from the Charlotte and Monroe County Fire Departments have deployed to Anson County to assist in the emergency response.•	A portion of a roadway – Hailey’s Ferry Road – was closed as a result of this incident. •	An evacuation of the immediate vicinity has been reported.https://twitter.com/wxbrad/status/1041505385788698624

properties.Description: Impacts: per NWS https://water.weather.gov/ahps2/hydrograph.php?wfo=ilm&gage=bgwn722.4' 12 miles of Highway 53 are underwater,in some cases 7 feet deep, between the Northeast Cape Fear bridge and Maple Hill. All homes including 60 in River Bend, 20 to 25 in River Birch and 12 in the Alligator Lake subdivision are flooded. 20 to 30 homes in Holly Shelter estates are underwater. In the Sandy Bend subdivision, off Shaw Highway, 40 to 50 homes, which is half of the homes in the subdivision sustain flooding. Portions of Croomsbridge, Island Creek and White Stocking Roads are underwater.16.5' White Stocking Road is closed and floodwaters begin to get into the homes in this area. Highway 53 is closed adjacent to the river. Stag Park Road has water 2 feet deep on it and becomes impassable.16	Water begins to get into homes, including those that are elevated, in the River Birch and River Bend subdivisions. Floodwaters also get into homes on Croomsbridge Road.15.25	The approaches to the bridge at Lanes Ferry on Highway 210 may be flooded. Much of White Stocking Road is closed. At the wildlife ramp on Shaw Highway, ramp is underwater and parking lot is half full of water.

properties.Description: severe storm surge inundation and coastal debris following Super Typhoon Sinlaku (April 2026). The roadway is almost entirely covered in thick sand and coral washed over the sea wall, with large mounds of debris pushed to the shoulder by clearing crews.

properties.Description: A Department of Public Works (DPW) crew using a Hyundai front loader to clear thick layers of sand and coral debris from the highway following the storm surge. Route 1 (Marine Corps Drive) in East Hagatna, Guam, looking South toward the capital.
properties.Title: Department of Public Works (DPW) crew removing debris on S Marine Corps Dr
properties.volunteer_note:
Mobil Oil Guam Corporate Office: The two-story white and grey building on the left is the headquarters for Mobil Oil Guam (located at 642 E Marine Corps Dr).

Agana Heights Cliffline: The prominent green cliff in the background is San Ramon Hill, with the residential buildings of The Cliff condos visible at the top.

Mobil East Agana Station: You can see the blue signage of the Mobil East Agana service station further down the road in the background on the left.

Streetview image https://tinyurl.com/k66s7hdd

properties.Description: Route 1 (Marine Corps Drive), East Hagatna: Storm surge pushed sand and coral debris across all four lanes. The stretch from Alupang Beach Tower to Anigua remains completely impassable, illustrating high coastal inundation risk in this low-lying zone
properties.Title: Debris and sand across S Marine Corps Dr near Guam Waterworks
properties.volunteer_note:
Landmark Triangulation: The red-roofed pavilion is a signature feature of Padre Palomo Beach Park (Trinchera Beach). Its proximity to the shoreline on the right immediately placed the camera on the southbound lanes of Route 1.

The Street Light "Anchor": To find the precise camera position, I looked for the vertical alignment of foreground and background objects. In the photo, a specific modern LED street light on a concrete utility pole appears perfectly centered "over" the peak of the gazebo.

Street View Verification: https://tinyurl.com/yjk8b4hv

properties.Description: Captures a dramatic scene along Marine Corps Drive (Route 1) in East Hagåtña, Guam,   Shows storm surge having pushed coral, sand, and ocean debris across the highway.
properties.Title: Debris and storm surge across Rte 1 near Mobil Station, Guam
properties.volunteer_note:
Key Landmarks
Mobil East Hagåtña: The gas station on the right side of the road is the Mobil service station located at 620 East Marine Corps Drive.

Alupang Beach Tower: The prominent white high-rise building visible in the far distance (at the top center-left of the bay) is the Alupang Beach Tower, located in Tamuning.

Hagåtña Bay: The body of water on the left is Hagåtña Bay. The image shows the storm surge having pushed coral, sand, and ocean debris across the highway, which is a common occurrence on this low-lying stretch of road during major typhoons.

Agana Heights Cliff: The steep green hillside on the right is part of the cliffline that leads up to the village of Agana Heights.

properties.volunteer_note:
Geolocation based on clues in the photo: fallen tree, a 35‑mph Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD) speed‑limit sign, utility poles, palm vegetation, and commercial buildings along a multi‑lane road. The photo was taken on the side of the FHP Health Center, with the vacant parking lot to the right belonging to FHP, although it is not visible in the image. The roadway to the left continues toward the Atkins Kroll car dealership on the opposite side of the road. These contextual landmarks confirm the general location, but since they are not visible, the photo is submitted at neighborhood/street level for accuracy. 

Contextual storm information was taken from the PostGuam article ‘Guam Recovering from Bavi’; the article did not contain this photo.

properties.how_did_you_geolocate_this_phot_other: Matched the stone breakwater, ocean exposure, heavy equipment, and layout to Kaumālapa‘u Harbor using Google Maps and the Hawaii News Now article showing almost the same repair site.
properties.volunteer_note: epairs underway to reopen Kaumālapa‘u Harbor following storm damage. Excavator and crew working on the outer breakwater structure.
